qualifying_findings.source_title: OpenCodeReview: Determinism over Non-Determinism for Cost-Effective Agent-Based Code Review
qualifying_findings.visible_date: Submitted on 10 Aug 2026; v1 Mon, 10 Aug 2026 08:43:16 UTC
qualifying_findings.date_qualification: In-window because the v1 submission time is after 2026-08-10T00:30:48Z.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The paper argues that LLM code-review agents suffer from unstable outcomes under unbounded tool use and from diff-local context. It proposes deterministic review stages: rule-guided dispatch, grounded file review with curated tools and ReAct, file-level parallel subagents, and independent reflection under an asymmetric information boundary. On AACR-Bench, it reports up to 2.17x higher SEM-F1 and 5-15x lower token use than mainstream coding agents across six backends.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The result supports deterministic review routing, bounded tool surfaces, independent falsification, and token-aware review architecture as practical design criteria for AI code review rather than relying on free-form autonomous review.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Local wiki should capture review-loop architecture implications: deterministic dispatch, curated retrieval/tool use, subagent boundaries, and independent reflection as eval-backed code-review practices.
follow_up_notes: During ingest, compare with intelligent code review, layered AI code review roles, code-review evals, and trajectory-level agent evaluation pages.
Consider routing broad benchmark/entity details upstream.

qualifying_findings.source_title: A Unified Issue Resolution Benchmark for Requirement Clarification, Planning, and Code Generation for Coding Agents
qualifying_findings.visible_date: Submitted on 10 Aug 2026; v1 Mon, 10 Aug 2026 03:22:04 UTC
qualifying_findings.date_qualification: In-window because the v1 submission time is after 2026-08-10T00:30:48Z.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: The SWE-RPG benchmark adds intermediate ground-truth references for requirement clarification and implementation planning to repository-level issue resolution. It includes 163 tasks from 31 Python and Java repositories and reports an average resolved rate of 31.5% for evaluated coding agents, with implicit requirement recovery identified as a major bottleneck in 24.5%-46.0% of runs.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The paper supports evaluating agent trajectories before the final patch: requirement recovery and planning need their own evidence, rubrics, and review gates because pass/fail tests alone cannot explain where agent work diverged.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Candidate local synthesis belongs in verification/evals and prompt/instruction practice: executable issue-resolution loops should preserve requirement clarification and implementation-plan evidence before code generation.
follow_up_notes: Check verification loops, trajectory-level evaluation, and request-package pages during ingest.
Route model and benchmark encyclopedia details upstream while keeping local trajectory-diagnosis practice.
